{{nihongo|'''Ikune Shrine'''|生根神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Settsu Province]].

'''Ikune Shrine''' (いくねじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} located in Sumiyoshi, {{ill|Sumiyoshi-ku, Osaka|ar|سومييوشي-كو|ca|Sumiyoshi|eo|Kvartalo Sumijoŝi|es|Sumiyoshi-ku (Osaka)|fa|سومی‌یوشی، اوساکا|fi|Sumiyoshi-ku|fr|Sumiyoshi-ku|it|Sumiyoshi-ku|ja|住吉区|ko|스미요시구|pl|Sumiyoshi (Osaka)|sco|Sumiyoshi-ku, Osaka|th|เขตซูมิโยชิ|tr|Sumiyoshi|zh|住吉區|zh_yue|住吉區|qid=Q985702}}, {{ill|Osaka|Q35765|qid=Q35765}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} (major shrine), and under the {{ill|Q712534|lt=former shrine ranking system}} it was classified as a {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}}. In the past, it was a subsidiary shrine of {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|Q705949|qid=Q705949}}. It is commonly known as “Oku no Tenjin” or “Okutenjin.”

=== Enshrined deity ===
* Principal deity – {{ill|Sukunabikona|Q3275687|qid=Q3275687|lt=Sukunahikona no Mikoto}}

Regarding the enshrined deity, works such as the '{{ill|Settsu Meisho Zue|ja|摂津名所図会|qid=Q11498549}}' and 'Sumiyoshi Meishō Zue' identify it as Sukunahikona no Mikoto, while the '{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō Studies|ja|神名帳考証|qid=Q11588824}}' presents a theory that it is {{ill|Ikutsuhikone|Q11147583|qid=Q11147583|lt=Ikutsuhikone no Mikoto}}{{Sfn|Shikinaisha Research Association|1977}}.

=== History ===
The precise date of foundation is unknown<ref name="由緒書">Shrine history leaflet</ref>. According to shrine tradition, it predates the founding of {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|Q705949|qid=Q705949}}{{Sfn|Shikinaisha Research Association|1977}}, but the '{{ill|Sumiyoshi Taisha Shrine Chronicles|Q11381815|qid=Q11381815}}' contains no mention of this shrine{{Sfn|Shikinaisha Research Association|1977}}. However, according to ancient tradition, since the shrine’s deity Sukunahikona no Mikoto is regarded as a god of sake brewing, {{ill|Empress Jingū|Q232803|qid=Q232803}} is said to have brewed sake at this shrine and offered it to the {{ill|Sumiyoshi sanjin|Q1114013|qid=Q1114013}}<ref name="御由緒">{{Cite web |url=http://ikune.a.la9.jp/history |title=Shrine History |publisher=Ikune Shrine |access-date=2024-02-27}}</ref>.

According to a document dated the first year of {{ill|Daidō|de|Daidō (Ära)|es|Daidō|fa|دایدو (دوره)|fr|Ère Daidō|ia|Daido|id|Daidō|ja|大同 (日本)|ko|다이도 (일본)|ru|Дайдо (нэнго)|simple|Daidō|sr|Даидо|th|ไดโด|tr|Daidō|uk|Дайдо|zh|大同 (日本)|zh_yue|大同 (日本)|qid=Q1373191|lt=Daido}} ({{ill|806|ab|806|af|806|als|806|am|806 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|806|ar|806|ary|806|ast|806|az|806|azb|۸۰۶ (میلادی)|bar|806|bcl|806|be|806|be_x_old|806|bg|806|bn|৮০৬|bpy|মারি ৮০৬|br|806|bs|806.|ca|806|cdo|806 nièng|ceb|806|ckb|٨٠٦|crh|806|cs|806|csb|806|cv|806|cy|806|da|806|de|806|el|806|eml|806|eo|806|es|806|et|806|eu|806|fa|۸۰۶ (میلادی)|fi|806|fo|806|fr|806|frr|806|fy|806|ga|806|gan|806年|gd|806|gl|806|he|806|hi|806|hr|806.|ht|806 (almanak jilyen)|hu|806|hy|806|id|806|ilo|806|io|806|is|806|it|806|ja|806年|jv|806|ka|806|kaa|806|kk|806 жыл|ko|806년|la|806|lb|806|lij|806|lmo|806|lt|806 m.|lv|806. gads|map_bms|806|mdf|806|mg|806|mhr|806|mk|806|mr|इ.स. ८०६|mrj|806 и|ms|806|mzn|۸۰۶|nah|806|nap|806|nds|806|new|सन् ८०६|nl|806|nn|806|no|806|nrm|806|nso|806|oc|806|or|୮୦୬|os|806-æм аз|pl|806|pt|806|qu|806|ro|806|ru|806 год|rue|806|sa|८०६|scn|806|sd|806ع|se|806|sh|806.|shn|806|si|806|sk|806|sl|806|smn|806|sq|806|sr|806|su|806|sv|806|sw|806|tg|Соли 806|th|พ.ศ. 1349|tk|806|tl|806|tly|806|tr|806|tt|806 ел|uk|806|ur|806ء|uz|806|vec|806|vi|806|vls|806|war|806|wuu|806年|xmf|806|zh|806年|zh_min_nan|806 nî|zh_yue|806年|qid=Q30021}}) in the '{{ill|Shinshō Kyakuchokufushō|ja|新抄格勅符抄|qid=Q11502312}}', one household from {{ill|Yamato Province|Q907495|qid=Q907495}} was assigned as a {{ill|Kanbe (social class)|Q11589711|qid=Q11589711}} to “Ikune no Kami” at that time{{Sfn|Heibonsha Regional Data Center|1986}}.

In the '{{ill|Engishiki|ar|إنجيشيكي (كتاب ياباني)|de|Engishiki|es|Engishiki|fr|Engishiki|he|אנגישיקי|id|Engishiki|it|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|ko|엔기시키|min|Engishiki|mr|इंगिशिकी|nl|Engishiki|pt|Engishiki|ru|Энгисики|simple|Engishiki|tr|Engishiki|uk|Енґісікі|zh|延喜式|qid=Q1342448}}' {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Register of Deities}}, compiled in the fifth year of {{ill|Enchō|Q1327274|qid=Q1327274|lt=Engi}} ({{ill|927|Q30470|qid=Q30470}}), the shrine is listed as “Ikune Shrine, Major, Tsukinami and Niiname,” under {{ill|Sumiyoshi district|ja|住吉郡|zh|住吉郡|qid=Q10885872}} of {{ill|Settsu Province|ca|Província de Settsu|cs|Provincie Seccu|de|Provinz Settsu|eo|Provinco Seccu|es|Provincia de Settsu|fa|ولایت ستسو|fr|Province de Settsu|gl|Provincia de Settsu|hak|Settsu-koet|id|Provinsi Settsu|it|Settsu (provincia)|ja|摂津国|ko|셋쓰국|lt|Seccu žemė|nl|Settsu (provincie)|pt|Província de Settsu|ru|Сэтцу (провинция)|simple|Settsu Province|sk|Seccu (provincia)|sr|Провинција Сецу|tr|Settsu (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Сеццу|zh|攝津國|zh_min_nan|Settu-kok|zh_yue|攝津國|qid=Q864163}}, placing it among the {{ill|Shikinai Taisha|ja|式内大社|simple|Shikinai Taisha|qid=Q134917288}}. It also records that the shrine received offerings at the imperial court’s {{ill|Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|Q11516161|qid=Q11516161}} and {{ill|Niiname-no-Matsuri|Q11501518|qid=Q11501518}}{{Sfn|Heibonsha Regional Data Center|1986}}.

In the 14th year of {{ill|Bunmei|Q1193544|qid=Q1193544|lt=Bunmei}} ({{ill|1482|Q6633|qid=Q6633}}), a Tenmangū shrine was established within the precincts. As this Tenmangū attracted popular devotion, Ikune Shrine itself came to be commonly known as “Oku no Tenjin.” The term “Oku” (“inner” or “deep”) derives from its location farther inland than {{ill|Daikai Shrine|Q11437478|qid=Q11437478}} when viewed from Sumiyoshi Taisha{{Sfn|Shikinaisha Research Association|1977}}{{Sfn|Heibonsha Regional Data Center|1986}}. Alternatively, the name is also said to originate from “Oki no Amatsu-kami” (the offshore heavenly deity, Sukunahikona no Mikoto)<ref name="御由緒" />.

From the 5th year of {{ill|Keichō|Q1328185|qid=Q1328185}} ({{ill|1600|Q6720|qid=Q6720}}) to around the 6th year ({{ill|1601|Q6725|qid=Q6725}}), the main hall was rebuilt through a donation by {{ill|Yodo-dono|Q247408|qid=Q247408}}, with {{ill|Katagiri Katsumoto|Q1882775|qid=Q1882775}} serving as magistrate<ref name="生根（いくね）神社">{{Cite web |url=https://www.city.osaka.lg.jp/kensetsu/page/0000009350.html |publisher=Osaka City |title=Ikune Shrine (Oku no Tenjin), Tangible Cultural Property of Osaka Prefecture |access-date=2024-02-27}}</ref>{{Sfn|Heibonsha Regional Data Center|1986}}.

During the {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}}, the shrine functioned as a subsidiary shrine of Sumiyoshi Taisha{{Sfn|Heibonsha Regional Data Center|1986}}. The 'Sumiyoshi Matsuba Taiki' records it in the section on subsidiary shrines as “Okutenjin Shrine,” noting that shrine monks from the {{ill|Jingū-ji|Q1074971|qid=Q1074971}} of Sumiyoshi served there{{Sfn|Shikinaisha Research Association|1977}}.

In {{ill|1872|Q7753|qid=Q7753}} (the 5th year of {{ill|Meiji era|ar|فترة مييجي|ast|Dómina Meiji|az|Meydzi dövrü|azb|مئی‌جی دؤورو|be|Перыяд Мэйдзі|bn|মেইজি যুগ|bo|མེའི་ཇིའི་དུས་དུས་མཚམས།|ca|Era Meiji|cs|Období Meidži|da|Meiji-perioden|de|Meiji-Zeit|el|Μεϊτζί (περίοδος)|es|Era Meiji|et|Meiji periood|eu|Meiji Aroa|fa|دوره میجی|fi|Meiji-kausi|fr|Ère Meiji|gl|Período Meiji|he|תקופת מייג'י|hr|Meiji (razdoblje)|ht|Epòk Meiji|hu|Meidzsi-kor|id|Zaman Meiji|io|Ero Meiji|is|Meiji-tímabilið|it|Periodo Meiji|ja|明治|ka|მეიძის ეპოქა|kbp|Mejii wɛɛ yaa alɩwaatʊ|kk|Мэйдзи дәуірі|ko|메이지 시대|la|Aetas Meiji|lt|Meidži laikotarpis|lv|Meidzi periods|mk|Меиџи (период)|mn|Мэйжийн эрин|ms|Zaman Meiji|nl|Meijiperiode|nn|Meiji|no|Meiji-perioden|pl|Meiji (okres)|pt|Era Meiji|ro|Perioada Meiji|ru|Мэйдзи|simple|Meiji period|sk|Obdobie Meidži|sq|Periudha Meixhi|sr|Меиџи период|sv|Meijiperioden|ta|மெய்சி காலம்|th|ยุคเมจิ|tl|Panahong Meiji|tr|Meiji Dönemi|uk|Період Мейдзі|ur|میجی دور|vi|Thời kỳ Minh Trị|war|Panahon Meiji|wuu|明治|zh|明治|zh_classical|明治|zh_min_nan|Bêng-tī|zh_yue|明治|qid=Q3125096}}), the shrine became independent from Sumiyoshi Taisha and was ranked as a {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}} under the {{ill|Q712534|lt=Modern shrine ranking system}}{{Sfn|Heibonsha Regional Data Center|1986}}. Between {{ill|1907|Q2048|qid=Q2048}} (Meiji 40) and {{ill|1911|ab|1911|af|1911|als|1911|am|1911 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|1911|ar|1911|ary|1911|arz|1911|ast|1911|av|1911|avk|1911|ay|1911|az|1911|azb|۱۹۱۱ (میلادی)|ba|1911 йыл|ban|1911|bar|1911|bat_smg|1911|bcl|1911|be|1911|be_x_old|1911|bg|1911|bh|1911|bn|১৯১১|bpy|মারি ১৯১১|br|1911|bs|1911.|ca|1911|cdo|1911 nièng|ce|1911 шо|ceb|1911|ckb|١٩١١|co|1911|crh|1911|cs|1911|csb|1911|cv|1911|cy|1911|da|1911|de|1911|diq|1911|dsb|1911|el|1911|eml|1911|eo|1911|es|1911|et|1911|eu|1911|ext|1911|fa|۱۹۱۱|fi|1911|fiu_vro|1911|fo|1911|fr|1911|frp|1911|frr|1911|fur|1911|fy|1911|ga|1911|gag|1911|gan|1911年|gcr|1911|gd|1911|gl|1911|gn|1911|gv|1911|hak|1911-ngièn|he|1911|hi|१९११|hif|1911|hr|1911.|hsb|1911|ht|1911 (almanak gregoryen)|hu|1911|hy|1911|hyw|1911 թուական|ia|1911|id|1911|ilo|1911|inh|1911 шу|io|1911|is|1911|it|1911|ja|1911年|jbo|1911moi|jv|1911|ka|1911|kaa|1911|kbp|1911|kk|1911 жыл|kn|೧೯೧೧|ko|1911년|krc|1911 джыл|ksh|Joohr 1911|kv|1911-ӧд во|kw|1911|la|1911|lb|1911|lez|1911 йис|li|1911|lij|1911|lld|1911|lmo|1911|lt|1911 m.|lv|1911. gads|mai|१९११|map_bms|1911|mdf|1911|mg|1911|mhr|1911|mi|1911|min|1911|mk|1911|ml|1911|mn|1911 он|mr|इ.स. १९११|mrj|1911 и|ms|1911|my|၁၉၁၁|myv|1911 ие|mzn|۱۹۱۱|nah|1911|nap|1911|nds|1911|nds_nl|1911|new|ई सं १९११|nl|1911|nn|1911|no|1911|nov|1911|nrm|1911|nso|1911|oc|1911|olo|1911|or|୧୯୧୧|os|1911-æм аз|pa|1911|pam|1911|pap|1911|pl|1911|pnb|1911|pt|1911|qu|1911|ro|1911|roa_tara|1911|ru|1911 год|rue|1911|sah|1911|sc|1911|scn|1911|sco|1911|sd|1911ع|se|1911|sh|1911.|shn|1911|si|1911|simple|1911|sk|1911|sl|1911|smn|1911|sq|1911|sr|1911|srn|1911|stq|1911|su|1911|sv|1911|sw|1911|szl|1911|ta|1911|te|1911|tet|1911|tg|Соли 1911|th|พ.ศ. 2454|tk|1911|tl|1911|tly|1911|tpi|1911|tr|1911|tt|1911 ел|ty|1911|udm|1911 ар|ug|1911 - يىلى|uk|1911|ur|1911ء|uz|1911|vec|1911|vi|1911|vls|1911|vo|1911|wa|1911|war|1911|xmf|1911|yi|1911|za|1911 nienz|zea|1911|zh|1911年|zh_classical|一九一一年|zh_min_nan|1911 nî|zh_yue|1911年|qid=Q2076}} (Meiji 44), two Sae Shrines (both formerly unranked shrines), Ryūō Shrine (formerly unranked), and Tanekashi Shrine (formerly a {{ill|Son-sha|ja|村社|qid=Q134917284}}) were relocated into the precincts{{Sfn|Shikinaisha Research Association|1977}}.

Foundation stones from the former Hobashira Kannon Hall, which had been built during the period of {{ill|Shinbutsu-shūgō|Q2279088|qid=Q2279088}} (syncretism of Shinto and Buddhism), are preserved within the precincts<ref name="由緒書" />.

=== Shrine precincts ===
* Main Hall (Osaka Prefecture-designated tangible {{ill|Cultural Property (Japan)|Q858308|qid=Q858308}}) – Rebuilt from the 5th year of {{ill|Keichō|Q1328185|qid=Q1328185}} ({{ill|1600|Q6720|qid=Q6720}}) to around the 6th year ({{ill|1601|Q6725|qid=Q6725}}) by donation of {{ill|Yodo-dono|Q247408|qid=Q247408}}, with {{ill|Katagiri Katsumoto|Q1882775|qid=Q1882775}} as magistrate. Built in the {{ill|Nagare-zukuri|Q210684|qid=Q210684}} style, with a chidori karahafu gable on the front. The roof is {{ill|cypress bark roof|Q90373477|qid=Q90373477}} (cypress bark roofing). It preserves a complete {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Momoyama period}} architectural style{{Sfn|Shikinaisha Research Association|1977}}<ref name="御由緒" />.
* Worship Hall – Incorporates Momoyama-period architectural style; renovated in {{ill|1936|Q18649|qid=Q18649}} ({{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}} 11).
* Kōbaiden – Said to be a relocated corridor of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Silla-dera}} (Shinra-dera), the {{ill|Jingū-ji|Q1074971|qid=Q1074971}} of {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|Q705949|qid=Q705949}}{{Sfn|Shikinaisha Research Association|1977}}<ref name="由緒書" />.
* Shrine office
* West gate

=== Subsidiary shrines ===
'''Affiliated shrines'''
* Tenmangū (Sugawara Shrine) – The wooden seated statue of Tenjin ({{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|ar|سوغاوارا نو ميتشيزانه|br|Sugawara no Michizane|ckb|سوگاوارا نۆ میچیزانێ|de|Sugawara no Michizane|es|Sugawara no Michizane|fa|سوگاوارا نو میچی‌زانه|fi|Sugawara no Michizane|fr|Sugawara no Michizane|id|Sugawara no Michizane|it|Sugawara no Michizane|ja|菅原道真|kk|Сугавара но Митидзане|ko|스가와라노 미치자네|la|Sugawara no Michizane|ms|Sugawara no Michizane|nl|Sugawara no Michizane|nn|Sugawara no Michizane|pl|Michizane Sugawara|pt|Sugawara no Michizane|ru|Сугавара-но Митидзанэ|sh|Sugawara no Michizane|sv|Sugawara no Michizane|th|สึกาวาระ โนะ มิจิซาเนะ|tr|Sugawara no Michizane|uk|Суґавара но Мітідзане|zh|菅原道真|zh_classical|菅原道真|zh_min_nan|Sugawara no Mitizane|qid=Q382005}}), the sacred object, dates from the 14th year of {{ill|Bunmei|Q1193544|qid=Q1193544|lt=Bunmei}} ({{ill|1482|Q6633|qid=Q6633}}) and is designated an Osaka City tangible cultural property<ref name="木造天神坐像" /><ref name="御由緒" />.

=== Festivals ===
The following festivals are held annually at Ikune Shrine<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://ikune.a.la9.jp/event/index.html |title=Festivals and Events |publisher=Ikune Shrine |access-date=2016-05-22}}</ref><ref name="由緒書" />.
* Monthly Festival – 9th of every month
* New Year’s Day Festival – January 1
* Setsubun Festival – February
* Awashima Festival – April 1
* Tanabata Festival – July 7
* Summer Festival Eve – July 18
* Mikoshi Procession – July 19
* Annual Grand Festival – October 9
* Mikoshi Procession Festival – October
* Children’s Festival – October
* Shichi-Go-San pilgrimage – November
* Daikon Cooking Festival – December
* Year-end Festival – December 31

=== Cultural properties ===
=== Osaka Prefecture-designated tangible cultural properties ===
* Main Hall (structure) – Designated February 20, {{ill|1970|Q2474|qid=Q2474}} (Shōwa 45){{Efn2|name=一覧表}}.

=== Osaka City-designated tangible cultural properties ===
* Wooden seated statue of Tenjin (sculpture) – Sacred object of the Tenmangū in the precincts. Created in the 14th year of {{ill|Bunmei|Q1193544|qid=Q1193544|lt=Bunmei}} ({{ill|1482|Q6633|qid=Q6633}}) during the {{ill|Muromachi period|Q334845|qid=Q334845}}<ref name="木造天神坐像">{{Cite web |url=https://www.city.osaka.lg.jp/kyoiku/page/0000117460.html |title=Wooden Seated Statue of Tenjin |publisher=Osaka City |access-date=2016-05-22}}</ref>. Designated April 1, {{ill|2011|Q1994|qid=Q1994}} ({{ill|Heisei era|Q234510|qid=Q234510}} 23){{Efn2|name=一覧表|From the Osaka City file of the “List of Designated Cultural Properties in Osaka Prefecture.”}}.

=== Osaka City-designated preserved woodland ===
* The {{ill|Ilex integra|Q848316|qid=Q848316}} trees of Ikune Shrine – The entire precinct is designated as sacred forest.

=== Address ===
* 2-3-15 Sumiyoshi, Sumiyoshi Ward, Osaka City, Osaka Prefecture

=== Access ===
* About 11 minutes on foot from {{ill|Sumiyoshitaisha Station|Q7637174|qid=Q7637174}} on the {{ill|Nankai Main Line|Q59453|qid=Q59453}} of {{ill|Nankai Electric Railway|Q1188230|qid=Q1188230}}
* About 9 minutes on foot from {{ill|Kohama Station|Q6425907|qid=Q6425907}} on the Nankai Main Line
* About 9 minutes on foot from {{ill|Sumiyoshihigashi Station|Q7637175|qid=Q7637175}} on the {{ill|Koya Line|Q71986|qid=Q71986}}
* About 7 minutes on foot from {{ill|Kaminoki Station|Q11588649|qid=Q11588649}} on the {{ill|Hankai Uemachi Line|Q5648519|qid=Q5648519}}
* About 9 minutes on foot from {{ill|Higashi-Kohama Station|Q5753654|qid=Q5753654}} on the {{ill|Hankai Line|Q5648522|qid=Q5648522}}
* About 5 minutes on foot from {{ill|Sumiyoshi Station (Osaka)|Q7637170|qid=Q7637170}} on the Hankai Uemachi Line / Hankai Line
